industry.key: K. Professional, business and consumer services
industry.why: Neutral, carried; the sectors are split (Testing B, Recruitment D, the rest C) and carry the view. Relative strength B (27-Nov-26 against 25-Sep-26, not week on week; C prior). Kepler (26-Nov) likes testing and inspection (Bureau Veritas, a private equity approach) and Hatzius (Goldman, 22-Nov) sees early signs of AI weighing on the job market, which is one sector up and one down. No change.

sector.why: Overweight, carried, now with a house behind it: Kepler (Donneky, 26-Nov) says Bureau Veritas' private equity approach highlights a fragmented market where the top five hold 15% share; regulated, recurring, non-discretionary demand from large proven cases. Relative strength A (27-Nov-26 against 25-Sep-26, not week on week; B prior). Pool name Eurofins. Not A: one house and four stocks. Counter-case: testing volumes follow industrial activity if the margin keeps rolling over.

geography.why: Overweight, carried: the 15% inclusive US tariff on Switzerland is 'largely as expected' (Goldman, 25-Nov), Roche is Kepler's pharma top pick and 'the clear AI leader in pharma' (26-Nov), and the Swiss market's low-beta character is the rotation this row was set on; the Swiss National Bank and the franc were not read. Counter-case: the franc takes 2 to 3 points a year off a Swiss exporter's reported profit. Back to C if the SNB joins the hikers or the franc reverses.
